clue.text: Spooner's limited sleep for romance

indicators.note: the Reverend Spooner famously swapped the opening sounds of word pairs, so the phrase that follows gets its first sounds traded

parts.note: limited means short; it gives its SH sound to the second word and takes a K sound
kip is British slang for a nap; its K sound moves to the front of the first word

explanation.surface: Someone short of sleep is told to blame it on their love life.
explanation.walkthrough: SHORT KIP becomes COURT SHIP once the SH and K sounds trade places; kip is British slang for sleep.
explanation.definitionFit: Courtship is the period of wooing a partner, so it stands as a synonym for romance.

clue.text: Bird hit leaving lake

indicators.note: something leaving departs, so that letter goes out of the word it sat in

parts.note: to clock someone is British slang for hitting them
L is the standard abbreviation for lake

explanation.surface: A bird is struck and flies off from the lake.
explanation.walkthrough: CLOCK loses its L to leave COCK; clock meaning to punch is informal British usage.
explanation.definitionFit: A cock is a male bird, especially the adult male chicken, so it is an example of the general term.

clue.text: Across river entering one local

indicators.note: to enter is to go inside, so one piece is placed within another

parts.note: 'un is the dialect or local way of saying one
the Po is Italy's longest river, a crossword favourite

explanation.surface: Someone crosses a river into a neighbourhood pub, a local.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Local' looks like a pub, but here it marks a regional pronunciation of one, as in 'a good 'un'.
explanation.definitionFit: To come across something and to come upon it are the same idiom, meaning to find by chance.

clue.text: Finally issue blame in your former treatment

indicators.note: in places pieces inside an outer word that wraps around them

parts.note: thy is the old, former word for your

indicators.note: finally points to the end, so only the closing letter of the next word is kept

parts.note: the final letter of issue
to take the rap is to take the blame

explanation.surface: Someone finally blames the treatment they once received.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Your former' asks for the archaic word once used in place of your, as in hymns and the Bible.
explanation.definitionFit: Therapy is medical or psychological treatment for a condition, a direct synonym of the general word.

clue.text: Blag from good person after that man is half-cut

parts.note: he is the pronoun for that man

indicators.note: cut in half, a two-letter word keeps just one of its letters, the first

parts.note: the front half of is
ST, saint, is the crossword's good person

explanation.surface: A drunk man, half-cut, cadges something from a do-gooder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Half-cut' is British slang for drunk, but it trims is to I. 'After' places the saint after HE and I.
explanation.definitionFit: A blag is British slang for a robbery, so a heist, an armed theft, is a synonym.

clue.text: Soldier gathered with troops over boundary

parts.note: a para is a paratrooper
people who gathered met

indicators.note: over means turned over, so the letters are flipped round in this down light

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers

explanation.surface: A soldier rallies with his unit at the border.
explanation.walkthrough: RE, the Royal Engineers, is the usual crossword shorthand for troops; turned over it becomes ER at the foot.
explanation.definitionFit: A parameter is a limit that sets the scope of something, so it can mean a boundary.

clue.text: They illuminate subterranean bases

definitions.meaning: first meaning: glass light sources screwed into lamps
second meaning: the swollen underground stems from which tulips and onions grow

explanation.surface: Lights shining in underground military bases.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests lamps in bunkers; the second half is botany, the rounded root stock that sits in the soil.
explanation.definitionFit: Electric lamps and plant storage organs share one name, each sense matching one half of the clue.

clue.text: Group of cells round the bend I'm uncertain to enter

indicators.note: to enter is to go inside, so one piece goes within another

parts.note: round the bend and batty both mean mad
er is the hesitation noise of someone unsure

explanation.surface: Someone driven mad in a prison block, unsure what's going on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Group of cells' looks like a prison wing, but means electrical cells.
explanation.definitionFit: A battery is strictly a set of electrochemical cells connected together to provide power.

clue.text: Dispute is the very thing concealed by crude oil giant

indicators.note: something concealed is hidden inside, so one piece is wrapped by the other
crude means raw and unrefined, so the letters are left in a rough new order

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
'it' is the very thing, as in 'that's it'

explanation.surface: A legal row is just what a big oil company is hiding.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crude oil' reads as petroleum, but crude rearranges OIL GIANT into LIGATION, which then hides IT after its L.
explanation.definitionFit: Litigation is the process of taking a disagreement to court, so it is a legal form of dispute.

clue.text: See Prohibition man supporting case for some sobriety

indicators.note: in a down light a support holds things up from beneath, so what precedes sits on top of what follows
a case is the outside shell, so only the outer letters are kept

parts.note: the first and last letters of some
to see someone is to date them
Eliot Ness enforced Prohibition in 1920s Chicago

explanation.surface: A Prohibition agent defends keeping some people off drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'See' reads as a command to look, but it means to go out with someone. Eliot Ness was the American agent who fought bootleggers.
explanation.definitionFit: Sedateness is calm, serious composure, matching the wider sense of sobriety as gravity of manner.

clue.text: Form of fuel comprising hard block

indicators.note: to comprise is to include, so the outer word takes the other inside it

parts.note: coke is a solid fuel made from coal
H is the pencil marking for hard

explanation.surface: A solid fuel made of a hard block, like a briquette.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hard block' reads as a single object; it splits into the letter H and the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To choke a pipe or channel is to clog it, a verb synonym of block.

clue.text: Cross taken off when bishop comes in for mass

indicators.note: coming in for someone is replacing them, so one piece swaps out another

parts.note: to take someone off is to mimic them
RR, Right Reverend, is a bishop's title
M is the symbol for mass

explanation.surface: A crucifix is removed from church when the bishop arrives for Mass.
explanation.walkthrough: Cross, taken off, bishop and mass all suggest a church service. The Right Reverend, RR, replaces the M of IMITATED.
explanation.definitionFit: Cross as an adjective means annoyed, and irritated is a straightforward synonym for that state.

clue.text: Sportsperson began with wrongly securing headwear

indicators.note: to secure is to hold tight, so one piece holds another inside
something done wrongly is done out of order, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
a tam is a Scottish woollen bonnet

explanation.surface: An athlete started out wearing the wrong hat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Began with' looks like ordinary narrative but is the letter fodder, and the Scottish bonnet ends up inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A bantamweight is a boxer in a light weight class, so one kind of sportsperson.

clue.text: Activist group in rage being disruptive

parts.note: a camp is a faction, a group sharing a view

indicators.note: disruptive things break up order, so these letters are thrown into a new arrangement

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A protest group in a fury causing disruption.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Activist group' looks like one phrase, but the definition is the single word, and group is the faction CAMP.
explanation.definitionFit: A campaigner works actively for a political or social cause, which is what an activist does.

clue.text: Support workplace to set up American deal

indicators.note: set up in a down light means raised, so the letters read from bottom to top

parts.note: a lab is a laboratory, a scientist's workplace
US stands for American
to deal is to trade

explanation.surface: Backing a workplace scheme to set up a US business deal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Set up' reads as establishing something but here means turning upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A balustrade is a railing on posts along a staircase or balcony, a physical support to lean on.

clue.text: One tests aluminium buried in some stone

indicators.note: something buried lies inside the ground around it, so one piece goes within another

parts.note: any and some are interchangeable, as in 'have you any?'
Al is the chemical symbol for aluminium
st is the abbreviation for stone, a British weight of 14 pounds

explanation.surface: A scientist checks for traces of aluminium in a rock sample.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Some stone' reads as a rock but is two pieces, and the metal goes only inside the first; a stone is a British weight of 14 pounds.
explanation.definitionFit: An analyst examines samples or data in detail, so is a person whose job is testing.

clue.text: Bland mousse? Let's attack sandwiches on the counter

indicators.note: counter means against or opposite, so the letters run the other way
a sandwich holds a filling, so the letters needed lie held within these words

parts.note: the run from the second S of mousse to the T of attack

explanation.surface: A dull dessert prompts someone to attack the sandwiches on the café counter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sandwiches on the counter' paints a café display but means letters held inside, read backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Bland food has little flavour, and tasteless is the plain synonym for lacking flavour.

clue.text: Satellite boxes close to telly push the boundaries

indicators.note: to box something is to enclose it, so one piece goes inside another

parts.note: Triton is the largest moon of Neptune

indicators.note: the close of a word is its end, so just its last letter is used

parts.note: the final letter of telly

explanation.surface: A satellite TV box near the television is pushing its limits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Satellite' and 'telly' suggest a TV dish, but the satellite is a moon. Telly is British for television.
explanation.definitionFit: To try it on is a British idiom for testing how much one can get away with.

clue.text: Beast having part of coat stripped

indicators.note: stripping removes the outer layer, so the first and last letters come away

parts.note: the folded flap at the front of a jacket

explanation.surface: An animal with part of its coat shaved off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Coat' suggests an animal's fur, but it is a jacket; LAPEL loses its outer letters to leave APE.
explanation.definitionFit: An ape is a primate such as a gorilla or chimpanzee, an example of an animal.

clue.text: Springs add power with little weight

parts.note: P is the symbol for power
ounces are small units of weight

explanation.surface: Metal springs give more force without adding much weight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Springs' looks like coils in a mechanism but is a verb: leaps.
explanation.definitionFit: A cat that pounces leaps suddenly onto its prey, so the verb matches springs as in jumps.

clue.text: Vessels advanced on France in midst of troubles

indicators.note: something in the midst of another sits in its middle, so one piece goes inside

parts.note: cares are worries or troubles
A is the abbreviation for advanced, as in A level
F is the international vehicle code for France

explanation.surface: Ships pushing towards France during a crisis.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Vessels' suggests boats on a voyage, but they are wine jugs; A and F go in the middle of CARES.
explanation.definitionFit: Carafes are glass jugs for serving water or wine, so they are a kind of container.

clue.text: Turned more elitist rejecting European bands

indicators.note: something turned faces the other way, so the letters run backwards
rejecting something throws it out, so a letter is dropped

parts.note: a snob is an elitist, so more elitist is snobbier
E is the abbreviation for European

explanation.surface: Someone grew snootier and snubbed European music groups.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bands' suggests musicians, but it is strips of material. Reversed SNOBBIER loses its E.
explanation.definitionFit: Ribbons are narrow strips of fabric, which is one meaning of bands.

clue.text: Rod and net that might be special

parts.note: a bar is a metal rod
to net money is to gain it

explanation.surface: A fishing rod and net that might be something special for an angler.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rod and net' paints fishing gear; 'and' simply joins the two pieces. Net is a verb here, to earn.
explanation.definitionFit: In shops a special is a discounted offer, which is a bargain.

clue.text: Agent at home with Word and electronic log

parts.note: someone at home is in
a term is a word or expression
E is short for electronic, as in email
a diary is a daily log

explanation.surface: A secret agent at home using Microsoft Word and an electronic diary.
explanation.walkthrough: The capital on 'Word' suggests the software, but it is just a synonym of term.
explanation.definitionFit: An agent acts on someone's behalf between parties, which is the role of an intermediary or go-between.

clue.text: One starkers removing article that's stained

indicators.note: removing takes something away, so those letters are dropped

parts.note: one is I, and starkers is British slang for naked
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A nudist strips off a garment that has a stain on it.
explanation.walkthrough: Starkers is British slang for stark naked. Dropping A from I NAKED leaves the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Paper or skin that has been inked is marked with ink, so it is stained.

clue.text: Drink when upset, guzzling excessive amount

indicators.note: to guzzle is to swallow greedily, so one piece takes another inside
upset means knocked over, so in a down light the letters are turned upwards

parts.note: as means when, as in 'as I left'
OD is an overdose

explanation.surface: Someone drinks too much when they are unhappy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Upset' and 'guzzling' paint a sad binge, but both are instructions on the short pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Soda is a fizzy soft beverage, so it is one kind of thing you drink.

clue.text: Reject hollow ruby lacking polish

parts.note: a den is a hollow or lair where an animal hides

indicators.note: lacking means without, so those letters are taken away

parts.note: taken as written
to rub is to polish

explanation.surface: A jeweller turns down a dull hollow ruby that has not been polished.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hollow' looks like an adjective emptying ruby, but it is a noun, the lair DEN; RUB is removed from ruby.
explanation.definitionFit: To deny a request is to refuse it, so the verb is a synonym of reject.

clue.text: One always ordered fare taken out to lunch

indicators.note: out to lunch is slang for crazy, so these letters go wild into a new order

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A regular diner who always orders the takeaway for lunch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ordered' looks like the anagram signal or a restaurant order, but it means tidy; the real signal is the slang 'out to lunch'.
explanation.definitionFit: A neat freak insists everything is tidy and in its place, someone who is always orderly.

clue.text: Too respectable for street filled with stench

indicators.note: something filled with stuff holds it inside, so one piece goes within another

parts.note: Ave is short for avenue, a street
BO is body odour

explanation.surface: A snob thinks themselves too good for a road that stinks.
explanation.walkthrough: BO, body odour, is the usual shorthand for a bad smell; it goes inside AVE.
explanation.definitionFit: To be above something is to consider oneself too good or proper to do it, an idiom.

clue.text: Drums very absent in festivities

indicators.note: absent means missing, so that letter is taken out of the word

parts.note: revels are lively celebrations
V is the abbreviation for very

explanation.surface: No drums are heard at the celebrations at all.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drums' suggests percussion, but these are cylinders that cable or thread winds round. REVELS loses V.
explanation.definitionFit: Reels are spools or cylinders for winding cable or film, which is a sense of drums.

clue.text: Inactive marine tracks gathering depression

indicators.note: to gather is to draw in, so the outer letters take the other piece inside

parts.note: marine means of the sea
RY is short for railway, the tracks
a dent is a small depression

explanation.surface: A lazy marine trudges along tracks, feeling depressed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Marine' looks like a soldier and 'depression' like low mood; both are plain synonyms, the sea and a hollow.
explanation.definitionFit: Sedentary describes a sitting, inactive way of life, a direct synonym of inactive.
